purpose: Resolve the independently attested PRIMARY_UPSTREAM_SELECTION blocker for PC-CROP #3785 by permitting one fail-closed web-bound Caddy upstream without exposing production topology.
requiredInvariants: The repair remains exact-main, canonical-DNS, absent-AAAA, pinned-SSH, owner-authorized and concurrency-guarded.
The exact-primary-host selector remains preferred and its selected dial must pass the same running-web shared-network identity binding as every fallback.

A fallback is permitted only when the exact-primary-host match count is zero and exactly one well-formed Caddy reverse-proxy dial is a per-network DNS alias of the single running Compose web container on a Docker network shared with Caddy.
A fallback with zero or multiple web-bound dials, multiple exact-primary-host dials, a network-unrelated alias, or any selected dial that is not web-bound must fail before backup or mutation.
Unrelated Caddy upstreams may coexist but no upstream value, alias, network, container ID, working path or secret may reach Actions output, artifacts, summaries or issue comments.
An already-enabled control route may return no-op success only when its persistent Compose wiring and sole marked reverse_proxy dial are revalidated against the newly selected current web upstream.
The original production Compose files remain unedited; the previously authorized fixed additive override is the only permitted gate-wiring repair.
The current immutable web image ID and OCI revision remain unchanged; only web may be recreated and every non-web container ID, including Caddy, remains unchanged.
Candidate Compose and Caddy configuration validate before mutation; internal and external rollback semantics remain unchanged.
Ten consecutive public acceptance rounds remain mandatory before success is published.
GO remains forbidden until reviewer MFA, First Customer and all 9 of 9 role journeys pass.
acceptance: Workflow YAML and all embedded remote Bash scripts parse before merge.
Static positive and negative fixtures prove one shared-network web alias is accepted while zero, two, and wrong-network candidates fail closed.
Read-only readiness reaches a READY_*_UNIQUE_WEB_BOUND_UPSTREAM_BEFORE_BACKUP state without publishing topology.

The guarded cutover reports PRIMARY_HOST_MATCH or UNIQUE_WEB_BOUND_UPSTREAM and passes TLS, control-login, host-isolation, parent redirect, API denial, exact-revision and primary-domain checks for 10 of 10 rounds.
Any pre-acceptance failure is either no-mutation or internally rolled back; any public-acceptance failure invokes the authenticated external rollback.
